title: TypeScript OOP versus JavaScript prototypes and C# classes
hook: TypeScript OOP versus JavaScript prototypes and C# classes shows up in everyday TypeScript and in senior interviews — this page explains what it is, why it matters, and how it behaves in the compiler versus JavaScript or C#.

blocks.text: TypeScript OOP versus JavaScript prototypes and C# classes is a core concept in TypeScript. At run time, types erase — the engine still executes JavaScript — but at compile time this concept shapes safe APIs and catches bugs before deploy. This page explains the idea in plain English first, then shows small, explained examples you can run in the browser console or Node.js.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and production code both probe whether you understand TypeScript OOP versus JavaScript prototypes and C# classes beyond syntax memorization. Misunderstanding here leads to subtle bugs — wrong equality results, leaked memory, untyped JSON boundaries, or async ordering surprises. If you know JavaScript, the comparison sections below help you transfer mental models instead of starting from zero.

blocks.title: Interview trap
blocks.body: Interviewers often ask "TypeScript OOP versus JavaScript prototypes and C# classes" as a follow-up to a coding exercise. They want mechanism and tradeoffs — not a one-line definition.
